title: Afaro data removal broker opt-out manifest
description: Describes one broker's public opt-out flow as data. A manifest never contains executable code. Every manifest records the public page it was built from, the date it was read, and a committed capture of that page.

id.description: Stable slug for this broker. Used in run logs and in the manifest filename.

name.description: Broker brand name as it appears on the site. Brands only, never parent companies.

search_url_template.description: The broker's public search interface, with profile placeholders in double braces. This is the same URL a person gets by using the site's own search box.

method.description: How the opt-out is filed. manual means the broker requires an account, a payment, a notarized document, or a government ID, and Afaro does not automate it.

profile_fields_required.description: Profile field paths this manifest reads, for example full_name or current_address.city. The orchestrator stops if any is missing rather than inventing a value.

recheck_after_days.description: The broker's stated processing window, in days, as written on the captured page. removal-verify waits this long before rechecking. null when the page states no window, which pairs with recheck_stated false and leaves the wait to the orchestrator's default.

notes.description: Anything the person needs to know that is visible on the captured page. Empty string when there is nothing to say.

source_url.description: The broker's public opt-out page this manifest was built from.

verified_on.description: The date source_url was read and captured, YYYY-MM-DD.

source_capture.description: Path to the committed screenshot of source_url, relative to the manifests directory. The validator fails if the file is absent.

recheck_stated.description: False when the captured page states no processing window. recheck_after_days is then null and the orchestrator falls back to its own default, saying the broker stated none. Absent or true means the number is the broker's own. Where the page that states it is not among the captures, because it appears only after a real submission, the notes say where it was read and that no capture exists yet.

name_page.description: A broker's own public name-directory landing page: a static page keyed by name, and sometimes by state or city, that the site publishes for search engines and public linking. Where one exists it is a cheaper and steadier door than the search box, and search-conduct.md carves it out of the result-URL ban under four conditions. It takes two captures and neither substitutes for the other: the site's own A-to-Z bar, which lists letters and names nobody, and the person's own name page from a real run, blanked like any run capture. A capture of a directory letter page is not one of them and never will be: those pages list strangers, and blanking a thousand names is not something anybody can check. Until a broker has both captures the block stays absent, and a pattern seen in a live search is a lead rather than provenance.

template.description: The page address with slug placeholders in double braces, for example https://example.com/people/{{name_slug}}/{{state_slug}}/. The same endpoint ban as search_url_template applies.

slug_rules.description: How each placeholder is built from the profile, in plain words, one entry per placeholder.

levels.description: Which pages the site publishes. A level that returns 404 where the site supports it is a not_found signal for that level, not an error.

directory_path.description: The links a person clicks to reach the page from the site's own directory, in order. This is what the capture shows, and it is what makes the pattern provenance rather than a guess.

shows.description: free_listing: the page shows the listing in the open and can settle found or not_found on its own. teaser: enough to match on name, age, and city with the rest hidden, which the scan treats as free_listing and says so. funnel: the page sells a report, settles nothing, and leaves the broker not_assessable unless another door works.

consent_modal.description: True when a terms or cookie wall stands in front of the page's content. The scan then stops there the way it does on a search page, and the person decides.

directory_capture.description: Path to the committed capture of the site's own A-to-Z name bar, relative to the manifests directory. Letters only. Nobody is named on it, which is why it may be committed at all. The validator fails if the file is absent.

page_capture.description: Path to the committed capture of the person's own name page, reached in a real run and blanked the way every run capture is. This is what shows the page exists and what it shows; the template is read from that page's own address and written here with the slugs put back as placeholders, so no name reaches the manifest or the run log. The validator fails if the file is absent, or if it is the same file as directory_capture.

additional_captures.description: Further pages this manifest was written from, beyond source_capture. A page reachable only inside a real run is captured by the person running it, with every value of theirs blanked, and listed here so each later step has a page behind it. The validator fails a manifest whose listed capture is absent on disk.

of.description: Which page this is, in plain words, and how it was reached.

blanked.description: True when values belonging to the person whose run produced the capture were painted out before it was committed, false when the page held nothing of anyone's. Required, because a capture from a real run that says nothing about blanking is the one a reader has to take on trust.

page_url.description: A public page over https. Loopback over http is allowed only for the checked-in smoke manifest, and the validator refuses it anywhere else.

selector.description: How to find the control on the page. Prefer the visible label. A CSS selector is a fallback that is expected to drift.

label.description: The visible text on the captured page. Must appear in the capture.

verification.description: How to tell later whether the listing is gone.

url_template.description: Required when method is status_page. Profile placeholders in double braces.

success_when.description: Plain description of what a removed listing looks like, taken from the captured page or from the search result page.

id_requirements.description: What the broker demands beyond the form. Any kind listed here makes this broker method manual.

step_handoff.description: The manifest stops here and the broker's flow does not. The person carries it the rest of the way in their own browser. Terminal: it is the last step, there is at most one, and the outcome for this broker is handed off at that step, never submitted. No recheck clock starts.

reason.description: page_not_captured: the rest of the flow was not on the public page this manifest was written from. requires_listing_url: the flow cannot go on without a listing URL that is not available. requires_email_link: the flow completes in a link the broker emails.

prompt.description: What is left for the person to do, in plain words.

step_accept_terms.description: A consent or terms dialog that stands in front of the flow. The selector names the control that declines, or consents to the least the dialog allows, because that is the choice Afaro makes. It comes before anything is filled and before the submit gate, and the validator holds it there.

selector.description: The decline control, or the minimal-consent control when the dialog has no decline.

warnings.description: What else the dialog does that the person should know about, as seen on the captured page. A control that opens a paid checkout goes here.

step_use_search_box.description: Search through the box the site shows, rather than through an address. This is what a broker gets when its search_url_template has drifted or was never a page: the box is typed into and submitted the way a person would. It comes before anything is filled on a form and before the submit gate, because a search is not a submission and must never be a way to send form values early.

url.description: The page holding the box, when the run is not already on it.

inputs.description: The boxes of the search form and what goes in each, in the order the page shows them.

submit.description: The control that runs the search. Absent means the form is submitted from the box itself.

step_find_listing.description: Identify the person's own listing in the broker's public search results. Never a direct result-endpoint URL.

value_from.description: Profile field path. The orchestrator stops if the field is missing.

value_literal.description: A fixed value the form needs, for example a reason code offered by the page itself. When the page offers a fixed set, list it in choices and this value has to be one of them.

format.description: How the value is written into the box, when the box wants it in a shape the profile does not keep. digits strips everything that is not a digit, which is what a phone field that rejects brackets and dashes needs. lowercase lowers the case. as_is is the default and is the same as leaving this out. The profile keeps the value as a person writes it; the step does the shaping, and the read-back afterwards checks the shaped value rather than the profile's.

choices.description: The options the captured page offers for this control, copied from it word for word. Present only when the capture shows them. The validator refuses a value_literal that is not one of these, which is what keeps a reason the broker never offered out of a form.

from_listing.description: Take the value from the listing an earlier find_listing step identified. The value never comes from the profile and never appears in a run log. url is that listing's address as the browser shows it; further attributes of the find_listing result are added here when a captured page asks for one. The validator refuses this without a find_listing step before it.

step_wait_for_email_confirm.description: The broker says it sends a confirmation email. The person opens it themselves.

step_read_email_confirm.description: Phase 1. Read the broker's confirmation email from the person's own connected mailbox and open the link. Defined here so Phase 1 adds behavior, not schema.

link_text.description: The visible text of the confirmation link, as described on the captured page.

step_human_gate.description: Hand the step to the person. reason submit is the guided-mode approval before anything is sent. The other four are steps no mode passes on its own.

gate_mode.description: combined folds the captcha gate immediately before this one into this prompt, so the person ticks, checks, and says go in one exchange. It exists for brokers whose captcha token expires inside the window between two separate gates, which turns a correct two-gate flow into a failed submission. Only valid on a submit gate, and only when a captcha gate is the step immediately before it. Absent means the two gates are asked separately, which stays the default.

prompt.description: What the person is being asked to do, in plain words.
